name: Tents
rules: Every tree needs its own tent directly beside it, never diagonally. Tents never touch, not even at corners. The numbers count the tents in each row and column.
technique.1: No tree next to this cell still needs a tent, so this cell can't hold one.
technique.2: A tent already touches this cell, so this cell can't hold one.
technique.3: This tree has only one cell left where its tent can go, so that cell must be a tent.
technique.4: This tree's tent must go in one of two cells, and both of them touch this cell, so this cell can't hold a tent.
technique.5: Try every way of fitting in the tents this row or column still needs, using only the highlighted cells and never letting two touch. Some of those cells come out the same every time, tent or empty, so fill them in.
technique.6: Try every way of fitting in the tents this row or column still needs, using only the highlighted cells in it. Some highlighted cells beside the line touch a tent every time, so they can't hold one.
technique.7: Leave out the cells that cannot hold a tent: no free tree beside them, or touching a tent. This row or column needs as many tents as it has cells left, so every one of them is a tent.
technique.8: This row or column already has all its tents, so no other cell in it can hold one.
demo.1: Every tree needs its own tent in a cell beside it. The numbers count the tents in each row and column.
demo.2: A tent goes directly beside its tree, above, below, left or right. Corners do not count, so these cells stay empty.
demo.3: This column needs one tent, and only one cell is left for it.
demo.4: Tents never touch, not even at a corner. These two do, so one of them has to move.
demo.5: Only one cell beside this tree is still free, so its tent goes there.
demo.6: Every tree has a tent beside it, no two tents touch, and the counts all match.
hint.noFreeTree.none: No tree sits directly above, below or beside the ? cell, so a tent there would have no tree to belong to.
hint.noFreeTree.one: The one tree beside the ? cell already has its own tent, so a tent in the ? cell would have no tree to belong to.
hint.noFreeTree.many: The {count} trees beside the ? cell all have their own tents already, so a tent in the ? cell would have no tree to belong to.
hint.tentTouches.one: The ? cell touches the outlined tent, and tents never touch, not even at a corner. So the ? cell can't hold a tent.
hint.tentTouches.many: The ? cell touches the outlined tents, and tents never touch, not even at a corner. So the ? cell can't hold a tent.
hint.treeNeedsTent: Every other cell beside the outlined tree is taken or ruled out, so its tent must go in the ? cell.
hint.treeCorner: The outlined tree's tent must go in one of the two outlined cells beside it, and both of them touch the ? cell. Whichever it is, the ? cell can't hold a tent.
hint.lineCount.row: Row {line}'s count is {count}. However you fit its missing tents into its empty cells, never letting two touch, each ? cell comes out the same every time, tent or no tent. So you can fill them in.
hint.lineNeighbour.row: Row {line}'s count is {count}. However you fit its missing tents into its empty cells, never letting two touch, one of them always touches each ? cell. So the ? cells can't hold a tent.
hint.lineExact.row: Every cell in row {line} except the ? cells already has a tent or can't hold one, and the row is still {missing} tents short. So every ? cell is a tent.
hint.lineExact.rowOne: Every cell in row {line} except the ? cell already has a tent or can't hold one, and the row is still one tent short. So the ? cell is a tent.
hint.lineFull.row: Row {line}'s count is {count}, and it already has that many tents. So none of the ? cells can hold one.
hint.lineFull.rowZero: Row {line}'s count is 0, so none of the ? cells can hold a tent.
hint.lineCount.column: Column {line}'s count is {count}. However you fit its missing tents into its empty cells, never letting two touch, each ? cell comes out the same every time, tent or no tent. So you can fill them in.
hint.lineNeighbour.column: Column {line}'s count is {count}. However you fit its missing tents into its empty cells, never letting two touch, one of them always touches each ? cell. So the ? cells can't hold a tent.
hint.lineExact.column: Every cell in column {line} except the ? cells already has a tent or can't hold one, and the column is still {missing} tents short. So every ? cell is a tent.
hint.lineExact.columnOne: Every cell in column {line} except the ? cell already has a tent or can't hold one, and the column is still one tent short. So the ? cell is a tent.
hint.lineFull.column: Column {line}'s count is {count}, and it already has that many tents. So none of the ? cells can hold one.
hint.lineFull.columnZero: Column {line}'s count is 0, so none of the ? cells can hold a tent.
